about: The built-in examples of the Universal Data Workbench. The page embeds each file; the synthetic tables are generated in the page from a fixed seed (src/examples.js).

pieces.title: Import and inspect
pieces.what: CSV and Parquet import on this device, a profile of every column, suspected data errors, suggested corrections that wait for approval, and the memory budget checked before each import.

pieces.title: Charts and candidates
pieces.what: Every valid chart of a documented grammar for each table, each accounted for as valid, excluded, failed or incomplete, with field, label, scale and layout edits.

pieces.title: Statistics and ranking
pieces.what: Two lists, unusual patterns and statistically supported patterns, with a test catalogue, Benjamini–Yekutieli adjusted p-values and six distinct highlights per list.

pieces.title: Publication figures
pieces.what: SVG, PDF and PNG at set sizes in millimetres, with general, Nature and Science presets and a check of each figure at its final size.

pieces.title: Export package and beamdswitch
pieces.what: One download with every valid figure, the report, the specifications, the statistics, a reproducibility manifest and a beamdswitch deck; projects save and reopen.

pieces.title: SQL and table algebra
pieces.what: A SQL editor and visual controls for joins, grouping, windows, pivot and unpivot, each recorded as a reproducible transformation.

pieces.title: Phones, speed and acceptance
pieces.what: Full-workflow tests on phones, a 1 million row benchmark, measured phone limits with a Measure this device button, and the acceptance checks.

examples.title: Planted patterns
examples.about: A synthetic table of 2,000 orders with patterns planted on purpose: a rare region, a cluster of unusual weights, a response that rises with dose, a group difference in score, a level shift in sales, -999 stand-ins in temperature, and identifiers written with leading zeros. Seed 20261005.
examples.licence: Generated by this page; no source data.

examples.title: A messy CSV
examples.about: A small synthetic CSV with the problems the import must report: a byte-order mark, a quoted line break, a short row and a long row, thousands separators, NA markers, an impossible date, dates whose day and month order is ambiguous, two date layouts in one column, -999 stand-ins and a value that is not a number.
examples.licence: Written for this page; no source data.

examples.title: Earthquakes of magnitude 5.5 or more in 2024
examples.about: Every earthquake of magnitude 5.5 or more worldwide in 2024, from the USGS earthquake catalogue, one row per event.
examples.publisher: U.S. Geological Survey, Earthquake Hazards Program
examples.licence: U.S. public domain: USGS-authored data are not subject to copyright in the United States.

examples.title: Daily weather in Central Park, New York, 2024
examples.about: Daily summaries of 2024 for the NY City Central Park station (GHCN-Daily USW00094728) from NOAA's National Centers for Environmental Information: precipitation, snow, snow depth, maximum and minimum temperature and wind, each with its measurement and quality flags.
examples.publisher: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
examples.licence: U.S. public domain: a work of the U.S. federal government (NOAA), not subject to copyright in the United States.
